subject.title: docs: LiteLLM supply chain attack advisory (v1.82.7 / v1.82.8)

question: What exact LiteLLM install version and remediation wording should OpenClaw recommend in the provider docs for users who may have run the reported compromised LiteLLM releases?
rationale: The docs surface and fix shape are narrow, but choosing third-party supply-chain remediation language and whether to pin new installs or only affected-version rollbacks requires security maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve updated advisory wording
options.body: Security maintainers choose current safe LiteLLM install and remediation text, then a focused docs PR updates `docs/providers/litellm.md`.

options.title: Document only general mitigation
options.body: The docs avoid naming a current safe install version and direct users to LiteLLM/PyPI advisories plus key rotation and host-audit steps.

options.title: Decline provider-specific advisory
options.body: Maintainers decide OpenClaw should not carry third-party LiteLLM incident guidance beyond linking to upstream security resources.

recommendation.title: Approve updated advisory wording
recommendation.body: Security maintainers choose current safe LiteLLM install and remediation text, then a focused docs PR updates `docs/providers/litellm.md`.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the adjacent supply-chain tracker that explicitly mentions this LiteLLM advisory and broader incident-response gaps.
